beats.title: Sinatra Sings Wee Small Hours
beats.description: A crooner's melancholy set of torch songs became an early showpiece for the album as a unified, brooding work.

beats.title: Elvis Presley's Debut Album
beats.description: A young Memphis singer's first LP became the first rock and roll album to reach number one on the US album chart.

beats.title: Miles Davis Records Kind of Blue
beats.description: A modal jazz session with a sextet became the best-selling jazz record of all time and a touchstone for every genre.

beats.title: Dylan's Freewheelin' Album
beats.description: A folk singer's second album mixed original songs of love and protest and made him the voice of a restless generation.

beats.title: Highway 61 Revisited Goes Electric
beats.description: A folk hero plugged in and opened an album with a six-minute rolling-stone epic that redefined what rock lyrics could be.

beats.title: The Beach Boys Release Pet Sounds
beats.description: A California band's studio-crafted masterpiece of lush orchestration pushed pop into art and inspired the Beatles.

beats.title: Sgt. Pepper Is Released
beats.description: The Beatles' studio-bound concept album, with its crowded cover collage, became the emblem of a summer of love.

beats.title: The Beatles Release the White Album
beats.description: A sprawling double album in a plain white sleeve gathered thirty songs of wildly varied styles from a fracturing band.

beats.title: Abbey Road Is Released
beats.description: The Beatles' last recorded album, with its medley and a zebra-crossing cover, became one of the most copied images in music.

beats.title: Bridge over Troubled Water Arrives
beats.description: A folk duo's final studio album sold in huge numbers and swept the biggest awards just as the pair went their own ways.

beats.title: Led Zeppelin IV Is Released
beats.description: An untitled record with four runic symbols on the label held the band's most famous song and became a hard rock landmark.

beats.title: Ziggy Stardust Lands on Earth
beats.description: David Bowie's story of an alien rock star made glam theatre mainstream and turned its creator into a cultural icon.

beats.title: Pink Floyd's Dark Side Is Released
beats.description: A prism on a black sleeve covered a seamless concept album that stayed on the charts for an astonishing length of time.

beats.title: Springsteen Releases Born to Run
beats.description: A New Jersey rocker poured his ambition into a wall-of-sound album about escape that made him a star overnight.

beats.title: The Eagles Release Hotel California
beats.description: A Californian band's dark allegory of excess, built around a twin-guitar epic, became one of the era's biggest sellers.

beats.title: Fleetwood Mac Releases Rumours
beats.description: A band recorded an album about its own breakups and betrayals, and it became one of the best-selling records ever.

beats.title: The Grease Soundtrack Album
beats.description: A film musical's soundtrack of rock and roll nostalgia became one of the best-selling soundtrack albums ever.

beats.title: Pink Floyd Builds The Wall
beats.description: A double concept album about isolation, with a schoolyard chant and a towering story of a rock star, filled stadiums.

beats.title: AC/DC Releases Back in Black
beats.description: A hard rock band's tribute to its late singer, with a new frontman, became one of the best-selling albums of all time.

beats.title: Michael Jackson Releases Thriller
beats.description: A pop star's seven-hit album and its cinematic videos made it the best-selling record in history.

beats.title: Prince Releases Purple Rain
beats.description: A Minneapolis star's soundtrack to his own film blended funk, rock and pop and made him a global superstar.

beats.title: Dire Straits' Brothers in Arms
beats.description: A British band's polished guitar record became a showcase for the compact disc and the first CD to sell a million copies.

beats.title: Beastie Boys' Licensed to Ill
beats.description: Three New York rappers mixed hip-hop with heavy metal riffs on a debut that became the first rap album to top the US charts.
beats.note: Released Nov 1986; reached number one in March 1987. Release year used.

beats.title: U2 Releases The Joshua Tree
beats.description: An Irish band's stadium-sized record of American landscapes and spiritual yearning made them the biggest group in the world.

beats.title: Madonna Releases Like a Prayer
beats.description: A pop star's boldest album mixed gospel, funk and confession, and its provocative title song caused a storm of controversy.

beats.title: Nirvana Releases Nevermind
beats.description: A Seattle trio's major-label album, with a swimming baby on the cover, knocked a pop king off the top and brought grunge mainstream.

beats.title: Dr. Dre Releases The Chronic
beats.description: A producer's solo debut introduced a smooth, synth-laden sound of West Coast hip-hop and launched a young rapper's career.

beats.title: Nas Releases Illmatic
beats.description: A young Queens rapper's compact debut, with tight verses over classic beats, became the benchmark for lyrical hip-hop.

beats.title: Alanis's Jagged Little Pill
beats.description: A Canadian singer's raw, angry confessional album sold in huge numbers and defined a wave of female-led rock.

beats.title: Radiohead Releases OK Computer
beats.description: An English band's anxious, futuristic record about technology and alienation was hailed as a landmark of its decade.

beats.title: Lauryn Hill's Miseducation
beats.description: A former Fugees star's solo debut fused soul, reggae and hip-hop and won a record haul of Grammy Awards.

beats.title: Radiohead Releases Kid A
beats.description: A rock band swapped guitars for synthesizers on a cold, experimental record that still went straight to number one.

beats.title: Norah Jones's Come Away with Me
beats.description: A quiet jazz-tinged debut from a young pianist became a surprise global hit and swept the Grammy Awards.

beats.title: Green Day Releases American Idiot
beats.description: A punk band's rock opera about disaffected youth revived its career and became a defining album of its time.

beats.title: Amy Winehouse's Back to Black
beats.description: A British soul singer's second album, steeped in retro sound and raw heartbreak, made her a global star.

beats.title: Radiohead Sells In Rainbows Online
beats.description: A major band let fans pay whatever they wanted to download its new album, upending how music was sold online.

beats.title: Adele Releases 21
beats.description: A British singer's heartbreak album of big ballads became a worldwide best-seller and swept the Grammy Awards.

beats.title: Beyonce Drops a Surprise Album
beats.description: A pop star released a full album with videos for every song, with no warning, rewriting how records are launched.

beats.title: Taylor Swift Goes Full Pop
beats.description: A country star's full leap to pop produced a chart-topping record of synth-driven hits and a major shift in her career.

beats.title: Kendrick's To Pimp a Butterfly
beats.description: A Compton rapper's dense, jazz-and-funk-inflected album on race and fame was hailed as a defining record of its decade.

beats.title: Beyonce Releases Lemonade
beats.description: A visual album spanning many genres, built around themes of betrayal and healing, premiered as a film before its release.

beats.title: Billie Eilish's Debut Album
beats.description: A teenage singer's whispery, bass-heavy debut from a bedroom studio swept the major Grammy Awards.

beats.title: Taylor Swift Drops Folklore
beats.description: A pop star announced and released a hushed, indie-folk album within a single day of lockdown, and it won the top Grammy.
